comments.author: @travellives
comments.text: If you live in Grenada, Carriacou or Petite Martinique, what has changed most in daily life since Beryl? We'd love to hear what people outside the islands often miss.

comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: Having to catch a boat at 7 in the morning just to get to secondary school makes the school commute feel completely different. I wonder how normal that feels to kids who grow up on Petite Martinique.

comments.author: @EpicEarthYTB
comments.text: Such an insightful documentary! It is truly inspiring to see the resilience of the people in Grenada, Carriacou, and Petite Martinique as they rebuild while keeping their vibrant culture alive.

comments.author: @TheHurricaneFile
comments.text: Focusing on Carriacou and Petite Martinique, rather than just the main island, is what makes this stand out — recovery there isn't a single rebuilding project, it's ordinary routines: repairing a roof, storing rainwater, getting children across the sea to school. That framing, starting with Grenada not being a single island, really shows how differently Beryl was felt across the islands.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Thank you so much for watching and for the kind words! 😊

comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: 😐🤨It's hard to imagine tourists enjoying the beaches while families on the smaller islands are still rebuilding after that hurricane. Anyone from Carriacou know how things are looking now? 🤔
